prompt:
Bug: household statistics fail since the SQLAlchemy 2.1 upgrade, and so does counting recipes by household.

GET /api/households/statistics answers 500 for every user. RepositoryGeneric.count_all(match_key, match_value) fails the same way when match_key names an attribute that is not a column of the model's own table. A recipe's household_id is one: recipes have no household column, the household comes through the recipe's user. SQLAlchemy reports that no FROM entity has a household_id property. Counting by a real column, such as group_id, still works.

Expected: GET /api/households/statistics answers 200 again. Its totalRecipes counts the recipes of the caller's household: a recipe created by a user raises that household's totalRecipes by exactly 1 and leaves the totalRecipes of another household in the same group unchanged. The other totals keep their meaning (users of the household; categories, tags and tools of the group). count_all filters on any attribute of the model, a column or one that comes through a relationship: on the unfiltered recipe repository, with two recipes created in a fresh group and household, count_all("group_id", group_id) and count_all("household_id", household_id) both return 2, and count_all("household_id", <unknown UUID>) returns 0. count_all() without arguments still counts everything.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests/repository_tests/test_recipe_repository.py tests/integration_tests/user_household_tests/test_household_self_service.py` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
